name: Seated Cable Lat Pulldown — Facing Away from Stack
description: A lat pulldown variation performed while seated facing away from the cable stack with a long bar or rope attached to the high pulley. The reversed orientation changes the angle of pull and places the shoulder in a different position relative to the resistance vector throughout the range, targeting the lower fibers of the latissimus dorsi and creating a unique stretch at the top position compared to a standard forward-facing pulldown. Used as a lat isolation variation to target different fibers and angles.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a bench or the floor facing away from a high cable pulley. Hold the bar or rope overhead with both hands and position the attachment just above and behind the head to create the reversed pull angle.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a straight bar or rope to the high pulley. Position a bench approximately 1-2 meters from the stack, facing away. The cable will pull from behind and above.
steps: Step 1: Sit facing away from the cable stack, holding the bar above head with arms extended.
Step 2: Depress and retract the shoulder blades, then pull the bar down toward the chest (bar will travel from behind-and-above to in-front-of-chest).
Step 3: Hold the contracted position with the bar at chest level, feeling the lower lat contraction.
Step 4: Slowly return to the starting position. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale during the pull. Inhale during the return.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward excessively to assist the pull — maintain an upright torso
Using momentum by swinging the torso
Allowing the cable to pull the arms too far back past a comfortable overhead range
safety_considerations: The cable angle creates a different shoulder loading pattern — start with light weight to assess comfort
Avoid if overhead extension causes shoulder impingement symptoms
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension of the arms overhead at the top to full contraction with the bar at chest level.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2s pull down, 1s contraction hold, 3s slow return.
coaching_cues: Depress the shoulder blades before you start the pull — do not shrug
Think of pulling the elbows down and forward toward your hip pockets
Feel the lower lats — this variation should produce a different pull sensation than a standard pulldown
